podcast.title: Live Radio Improv (1987)
podcast.body: In 1987, during an interview on live radio, Mojo Nixon improvised a song on the spot when asked why people should see him in a club instead of David Bowie in a stadium. "He picked up his guitar and improvised a song on the spot on live radio. And it was brilliant."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Honorary Winter Olympics Captain (1998)
podcast.body: In 1998, Mojo Nixon was bestowed the unique honor of being the honorary captain for the U.S. men's luge team at the Winter Olympics. "In 1998, Mojo Nixon was the honorary captain of the U.S. men's loose team for the Winter Olympics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death Details - February 7, 2024
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon passed away at the age of 66 on February 7th, 2024. He suffered a major cardiac event while performing on the Outlaw Country Cruise, with the ship docked in San Juan, Puerto Rico. "On February 7th, he was working as one of the performers on the outlaw country cruise. And he suffered a major cardiac event of some kind as the ship was docked in San Juan Puerto Rico."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Passing While Performing (Early 2024)
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon died while performing on a cruise ship in early 2024, a provision for which was not included in his rider. "Mojo died while performing on a cruise ship in early 2024."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Actor in Hollywood Films
podcast.body: In addition to his music career, Mojo Nixon also pursued acting, appearing in a number of Hollywood films. "Mojo also became an actor, appearing in a bunch of Hollywood films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Sylvia Massey
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon worked with producer Sylvia Massey, who later went on to work with the band Tool. "and he worked with Sylvia Massey, a producer who would later work with this band called Tool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Diverse Entertainment Career
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon remained active in the entertainment industry throughout his life, including a period where he pursued acting roles. "Mojo stayed in the entertainment business his whole life, even dipping into acting for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Partnership with Skid Roper (Late 1980s)
podcast.body: In the late 1980s, Mojo Nixon partnered with Skid Roper. Roper typically stayed in the background, playing various instruments he deemed appropriate, such as a washboard or a unique percussion device crafted from a mop handle and a laundry tub. "But when I first met Mojo, it was the late 1980s, and he was working with a partner named Skid Roper. Skid didn't say much. He kind of stayed in the background and played whatever instruments he felt was appropriate, like maybe a washboard or a weird percussion thing made from a mop handle and a laundry tub."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Political Stance and File Sharing Advocacy
podcast.body: He was a supporter of Democratic political candidates and was a vocal advocate for file sharing, notably during an era when Metallica was actively suing fans over the practice. "He supported Democratic candidates and was a big fan of file sharing in the era when Metallica was suing fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Psychobilly Style
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon was known for taking psychobilly in a fun and spontaneous direction, infusing it with an offbeat sense of humor. Psychobilly is a genre that blends punk, old-school rock and roll from the 1950s and early 1960s, rockabilly, and rhythm and blues. "Mojo took Psychobilly in a more fun and spontaneous direction, adding an offbeat sense of humor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Radio DJ Career
podcast.body: Nixon worked as a radio DJ in multiple cities, including San Diego and Cincinnati, and also on satellite radio. "He worked as a radio DJ in both San Diego and Cincinnati as well as on satellite radio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Very Reasonable Rider to Contract
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon, a rockabilly/punkabilly hero, was known for his "very reasonable rider." Its requirements included being nice (not beating up rowdy fans unless absolutely necessary), one case of Budweiser on ice (with a note for more if needed), a dressing room with a bathroom or four "P jars," and a couple of people to help carry equipment to and from the stage. This concise list constituted his entire rider. "That was the entire writer. Mojo died while performing on a cruise ship in early 2024."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Virginia Origin
podcast.body: Mojo Nixon originated from Virginia, where he found his niche in the psychobilly genre. "He came out of Virginia and found solace and a genre that became known as Psychobilly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
